user_reviews.Name: Jullian Agostinho
user_reviews.Description:
I’ve been coming to Pho Cue since early 2022. I used to go at least twice a month, so I feel like I can give a fair and honest review.

The food has consistently been one of the reasons I keep coming back. It’s still my favourite Vietnamese restaurant in Manchester. The original team was fantastic, especially the lady who used to welcome people at the door who no longer works there. She always made everyone feel looked after and was very agile handling big queues etc. There’s also another member of the original team who’s still there, and she’s always so friendly and welcoming. I genuinely enjoy it when she’s looking after my table.

A special mention also goes to Jason. I first met him when he was a waiter, and he always remembered me and my friends whenever we came back. That personal touch really makes a difference, and honestly, knowing Jason is still there is one of the reasons I continue to return.

That said, I also want to mention something that has disappointed me over the past couple of years. The gentleman who manages the queue has never been particularly welcoming. I completely understand the restaurant gets very busy. That’s not the issue. It’s more that this has become a pattern over several visits. He often comes across as though he’s doing customers a favour rather than welcoming them into the restaurant. Customer service is just as important as the food, and I think this is an area that could be improved.

As for the food, where do I start? The Vietnamese coffee is incredible. The pork spring rolls are an absolute must, and honestly, any of the salt and pepper or garlic butter dishes are excellent. If you’re not sure what to order, try the lamb chops or the beef with fried rice instead of jasmine rice (missing pics but I promise it’s worth it). You can thank me later. The BBQ duck is another favourite if you enjoy rich, saucy flavours, and the Special Pho is absolutely amazing.

Overall, I still think Pho Cue is well worth visiting. The food has kept me coming back for over four years, and that’s not something I say lightly. I just hope the front-of-house experience becomes as consistently good as the kitchen.

One final suggestion. Maybe consider closing at 10pm instead. 😅
user_reviews.text_original:
I’ve been coming to Pho Cue since early 2022. I used to go at least twice a month, so I feel like I can give a fair and honest review.

The food has consistently been one of the reasons I keep coming back. It’s still my favourite Vietnamese restaurant in Manchester. The original team was fantastic, especially the lady who used to welcome people at the door who no longer works there. She always made everyone feel looked after and was very agile handling big queues etc. There’s also another member of the original team who’s still there, and she’s always so friendly and welcoming. I genuinely enjoy it when she’s looking after my table.

A special mention also goes to Jason. I first met him when he was a waiter, and he always remembered me and my friends whenever we came back. That personal touch really makes a difference, and honestly, knowing Jason is still there is one of the reasons I continue to return.

That said, I also want to mention something that has disappointed me over the past couple of years. The gentleman who manages the queue has never been particularly welcoming. I completely understand the restaurant gets very busy. That’s not the issue. It’s more that this has become a pattern over several visits. He often comes across as though he’s doing customers a favour rather than welcoming them into the restaurant. Customer service is just as important as the food, and I think this is an area that could be improved.

As for the food, where do I start? The Vietnamese coffee is incredible. The pork spring rolls are an absolute must, and honestly, any of the salt and pepper or garlic butter dishes are excellent. If you’re not sure what to order, try the lamb chops or the beef with fried rice instead of jasmine rice (missing pics but I promise it’s worth it). You can thank me later. The BBQ duck is another favourite if you enjoy rich, saucy flavours, and the Special Pho is absolutely amazing.

Overall, I still think Pho Cue is well worth visiting. The food has kept me coming back for over four years, and that’s not something I say lightly. I just hope the front-of-house experience becomes as consistently good as the kitchen.

One final suggestion. Maybe consider closing at 10pm instead. 😅

Rather good traditional Vietnamese cafe opposite the Wing Yip on Oldham road.
The friendly but firm Quen ensures reasonably efficient service for the many regular diners.

First time we had a signature Bahn Mii which was amazing, perfectly toasted baguette stuffed with quality filling etc.
Second visit came back to try the Pho which was outstanding and at least on a par with the Bahn Mii.
Sizable bowl of delicious beef stock with a generous portion of rice noodles mixed beef - the obligatory side platter of lime, beansprouts, chilli and mint (had to ask for coriander which was obligingly delivered)
But sadly no sweet basil or saw tooth coriander.
All the same the meal was devoured and the bowl licked clean.  What more can I say!

user_reviews.Name: Antony Hunter
user_reviews.Description:
Whenever i come up to Manchester & stay in Northenden, I always visit @vietguymanchester for their fabulous and amazing authentic food and warm hospitality 😍😋👏🙌
I can certainly recommend the following dishes, which i had on this trip:
Papaya salad with prawns beautiful fresh papaya, mango, carrot, vegetables & prawns in a fresh dressing, I'm not lying when I say i could eat this every day for breakfast ❤️😋😋😋😋😋😋
Shaking beef, tender cooked beef with a crisp salad & dipping sauce 😋😋😋
Hot & sour soup with prawns, I love the fresh flavours of this soup, a hint of aniseed and a gentle warming heat, plenty of prawns 😋😋👍👌
Salt & pepper chicken wings, great textural change, lovely moist, juicy chicken wings in a stunning crispy coating 😍😋
Chicken curry with jasmine rice, exactly what it says on the tin, mild flavoursome curry with several chickens and a bucket load of veg (exaggeratedfor effect, but safe to say there is loads of chicken & veg), the rice shows it's all cooked with love ❤️😋😋
Accompanied by a few friends from Saigon and Hanoi 🍻🍻🍻😅🙈
Friendly service with a smile, and amazing food at a great value price 😍😍
You really must come and give them a try, you won't be disappointed, but be mindful they are popular, so if travelling I recommend you book 👍👌
Love these guys 👏👏🙌🙌🙌

user_reviews.Name: Hoàng
user_reviews.Description:
As an international student, finding a place that truly reminds me of home is priceless—and this restaurant does exactly that! The food here is absolutely authentic and full of flavor. I tried several dishes, and each one was amazing:
• The beef curry with turmeric rice was rich, creamy, and perfectly seasoned. The beef was tender, and the rice had a wonderful aroma with crispy shallots on top.
• The stir-fried noodles with chicken and vegetables were fresh and well-balanced, with just the right amount of crunch and seasoning.
• And of course, the pho was outstanding! The broth was clear yet packed with depth, the beef slices were fresh, and the herbs added that classic Vietnamese touch.
The portions are generous, the presentation is beautiful, and the atmosphere is cozy—perfect for anyone craving a taste of Vietnam. I highly recommend this place to anyone who loves authentic Vietnamese cuisine or wants to experience it for the first time. Definitely coming back!

I stumbled across this little gem in the heart of Manchester by chance, and I’m so glad I did. The restaurant is small but incredibly welcoming, with a warm and homely atmosphere.

The food instantly transported me back to Vietnam—authentic, flavourful, and every bit as delicious as I remember. The owner, Lý, is originally from Huế and embodies the warmth and hospitality of a Vietnamese mother. She is wonderfully friendly and makes every guest feel at home.

There’s also a small shop next door, offering a range of mostly homemade products, which adds to the authentic experience.

I would highly recommend this place, especially if you’ve never tried Vietnamese cuisine before. The only minor improvement I’d suggest is better ventilation, but aside from that, it’s a charming and genuinely homely spot that I’d happily visit again.

user_reviews.Name: G
user_reviews.Description:
Doux Chaton is an interesting spot. I only discovered it in Manchester by chance while walking past. I’d been to the Liverpool branch before and had mixed feelings, mostly because the service wasn’t great - the owner (middle aged woman not the elder lady, she’s lovely) there didn’t seem very accommodating, which left me a bit unsure about trying it again.

The Manchester branch was a better experience. We were welcomed by one of the female managers, who was super kind and friendly, so we felt like giving it a proper try. Another time, we were served by a friendly guy, but he seemed a bit lost and the ordering process wasn’t as smooth as we hoped.

The interior looks nice, very cafe-like and casual, which I liked. My only real shocker was the prices. A small bowl is £14.50 and a large is around £17. That’s pretty steep compared to places like Pho Cue, I Am Pho, or Ca Phe Viet, which are around £12 for a large. Plus, there’s a 12.5% service charge added and you have to pay upfront rather than after eating, feels quite extortionate and you’d never get this at any other Vietnamese restaurant in Manchester.

The pho itself is decent, but I still prefer the other spots I mentioned as they have more depth of flavor. I’ve tried a few other dishes here too, like the banh mi, which was a miss for me because the Maggi sauce overpowered the toppings. I also tried the Vietnamese coffee, both the salted and egg versions, and was let down, they came out bitter without the sweet notes you’d expect from Vietnam.

Overall, it’s an okay cafe to sit in and the service can be great at times, but I’d say the prices and some of the dishes don’t quite justify a repeat visit.

user_reviews.Description:
Service was attentive and swift. Atmosphere is impeccable good spacing and decoration and dont miss the beautiful wall painting they have. They play some lovely mix of pop music too.

I was slightly unsure when i saw the fusion menu because my past experience tells me that it usually isnt authentic. BUTTTTT it was authentic and i can say that as a fellow asian.

Waited around twenty minute which I didnt mind because it came fresh which I like. I did come early so there werent much people when I ordered. A lot of people did start coming in during lunch time and I guess that is a sign that its GOOD.

Not a lot of places offer nestled vermicile so that was my second sign. I got the chicken one and I loved the incorporation of greens. However I did find the chicken a bit dry for my likings. Flavours were insane the sauce dipping and whatever they use to marinate their chicken please keep doing that. They did a lunch deal EVEN on weekends so its 12 pounds with a viet drip coffee. Coffee was not as strong as I expected mb because it was a fusion place im not sure.

They also offer outdoor seating where I can see a lot of people were taking advantage of the good sun.

Would love to come back to try their pho!

user_reviews.Name: Pham Linh
user_reviews.Description:
such a gem in manchester. really impressed with their menu because not only do they serve traditional dishes but there were very creative dishes as well on the menu. i played it safe first so i just went with the vegan pho, stir fry pho, summer rolls, fried tofu. all were really decent in terms of taste and display!

- the vegan pho was hearty and light—some might say its bland but you can totally customize it by adding in hoisin or siracha sauce. it has a subtle umami from the veggies which was refreshing.
will try the creative dishes next time tho!
- summer rolls were on point—loved the sauceeee
- fried tofu is crispy on the outside and silky inside
- stir fry pho is okay, i feel like its a bit too oily
- additionally their drinks menu has a lot of interesting options with mixing tropical fruits

staffs are super friendly and helpful :)!

user_reviews.Name: Eric Chan
user_reviews.Description:
Pot Kettle Black is one of those places I’m generally happy to return to. The space is open, warm, and inviting, and it feels like a nice spot to slow down a bit, especially for brunch or a catch-up.

It does get pretty crowded on weekends, so expect a bit of noise and waiting around. Front-of-house service was prompt and friendly when we arrived, which helped, though the kitchen was noticeably slower. Food took a while to come out, but nothing outrageous, just something to be aware of if you’re in a rush.

Food itself was pretty decent across the board. Nothing overcomplicated, just well-executed brunch dishes that do what they’re meant to. The real standout for me was the coffee. Easily one of the better cups in Manchester. Balanced, well made, and clearly something they take seriously here. That alone makes the place worth coming back to.

Prices felt fair for the location and quality, especially given how central Barton Arcade is. You don’t feel like you’re being overcharged just for sitting somewhere trendy, which I appreciate.

Overall, it’s a nice, dependable place to meet friends, chat, and enjoy a good coffee. Go when you’re not in a rush, expect it to be busy on weekends, and you’ll likely leave feeling satisfied rather than stressed.

user_reviews.Name: Ramsha Bukhari
user_reviews.Description:
I left PKB feeling genuinely humiliated and unwelcome.

I visited at around 11am to get some work done and, as a paying customer, ordered food and a drink. I politely asked if I could move to a slightly bigger table so I had more space to work, but I was refused and told that the restaurant was “busy.”

What made the situation particularly uncomfortable was what happened next. Two men left one of the larger tables, so I moved over to it. The manager on duty — the woman with curly hair — then made me get up from the table, telling me that the men would be coming back.

They did not return while I was there. Instead, that same table was later given to another party.

There were also several other larger tables visibly unoccupied at the time, as shown in the photos I took during my visit and have attached to this review. I completely understand that restaurants need to manage their seating, but the way this was handled simply did not make sense to me and left me feeling singled out.

After I had finished and paid my bill, I calmly told the manager that the experience had made me feel discriminated against. There was no apology, no concern and no attempt to understand why I felt that way. Instead, she told me, “It’s fine, you can leave a bad review,” and then walked away.

That response was what made the experience even more upsetting. If a customer tells a manager that they feel they have been discriminated against, I would expect the concern to at least be taken seriously rather than dismissed.

I have lived in the UK for quite some time and have always found Manchester to be an incredibly diverse and welcoming city. This was the first time here that I left an establishment genuinely questioning whether I had been treated differently because of my background.

I won’t be returning, and I will be sharing my experience with others because I would never want anyone else to leave feeling the way I did.

You go to a café to spend your time, order food and drinks, pay for the experience and expect to be treated with basic courtesy and respect. You certainly don’t pay to leave feeling humiliated or singled out.

I’ve attached photos from around the time of my visit so people can see the circumstances for themselves and make their own judgement.

user_reviews.Name: Ace
user_reviews.Description:
I had the absolute pleasure of spending time in the Aspire Lounge at Manchester Airport Terminal 3 recently, and I can honestly say it completely transformed the whole airport experience.

From the moment I walked in, I was welcomed by friendly and professional staff who made the check-in process quick and effortless. The atmosphere inside the lounge is calm, modern, and well-maintained, offering a perfect escape from the busy terminal outside. It’s exactly what you want before a flight—comfortable, quiet, and relaxing.

The seating options were excellent, with plenty of space whether you want to unwind on your own, catch up on work, or sit together as a group. I particularly appreciated the cleanliness throughout the lounge; everything from the tables to the seating areas was spotless and clearly well looked after.

The food and drink selection was another highlight. There was a good variety of hot and cold options, all fresh and regularly replenished. The self-service bar was well stocked, offering a nice range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks, and the coffee machine was a lifesaver. It’s great being able to help yourself without long queues or waiting around.

One thing that really stood out to me was the overall ambience. It felt far more premium than expected, with soft lighting, a relaxed vibe, and just the right level of background noise. It made it easy to sit back, recharge, and genuinely enjoy the time before boarding.

Overall, the Aspire Lounge in Terminal 3 is fantastic value for money and a must if you want to start your journey stress-free. I’ll definitely be booking again for future trips—highly recommended!

user_reviews.Name: Eleanor Pollard
user_reviews.Description:
Went to the Aspire lounge in May before our morning flight, and we were really excited because it looks like such a lovely lounge compared to the other places to eat/sit in the old terminal. Sadly it was only okay.

On arrival the staff member welcoming us was exceptionally rude and snappy with us, and told us we might not be able to sit together as they were very busy (there were 4 of us, no accessibility needs/kids etc and the lounge was almost empty!)

We didn’t let the rude lady deter us from having a nice time as we usually really enjoy a lounge experience.

Some positives: windows!, really comfy seating, variety of types of seating, feels more cosy and private, nice and clean too (no dirty carpets), some staff working hard to clear tables etc. Also when one group of 4 men were being really loud the staff told them to be quiet and they did which was great. Food wise, nice granola, mini cereals, good sausages and bacon.

Negatives: much more limited food and drinks choices, no fresh orange juice, no prosecco available for a mimosa as part of the package (you have to pay extra), very limited breakfast options compared to the escape lounge, no pastries/fruit etc. When we asked if there was anything like this one staff member repeatedly told us they were so busy (not sure if something was happening behind the scenes because they lounge was less than half full at this point) and he brought us out a plate of muffins, and then when we were leaving they put out some pastries and fruit but this should have been available from the start. Scrambled eggs weren’t particularly nice and no toast/bread options, did have a pancake machine but it needed to be refilled after about 4 pancakes.

Overall just not the same quality food and drinks as you would hope for what you pay, but the comfort and views made it a somewhat pleasant experience. Probably would avoid flying from T3 until it is totally renovated to be honest!

user_reviews.Name: Gemma Montague
user_reviews.Description:
aving previously booked the Escape Lounge, we decided to try the Aspire Lounge this time as it looked much brighter and had plenty of natural light. Unfortunately, we were left disappointed.

One of the things I was most looking forward to was relaxing with a glass of Prosecco before my flight, but unlike the Escape Lounge, Prosecco is not included and comes at an additional cost. I then turned to the food offering and found the options extremely limited, with only soup or chilli available. So our options are to buy something from the limited menu or just go back to the main airport area. The WiFi doesnt work either.

As a result, it feels as though we've paid simply to sit in a bright room. While the Escape Lounge may have lacked natural light, it offered a better overall experience in terms of food and drink. Looking back, I wish we'd booked there instead.

Clearly the customer services don’t act on feedback, they’ve commented on every single one and yet my feedback is the same as feedback from months ago. Pointless. Try improving your food and drink options and you might start getting better reviews.

On a positive note, the staff were brilliant. Very polite, friendly and professional.

user_reviews.Name: Nadeem Bari
user_reviews.Description:
I’m writing this review while still waiting to get into the Aspire Lounge at Manchester Airport Terminal 2.

I joined the queue almost two hours ago, and after waiting all this time, it is still showing another 10 minutes.

I’ve had DragonPass for years and use it when travelling. At international airports, I normally get lounge access without much trouble. Manchester Terminal 2 has been a completely different experience.

For the last two years, I have not managed to get into Aspire or Escape at T2 using DragonPass. The only times I’ve been able to use these lounges have been when travelling Business Class and getting access through my ticket.

Today I’m travelling with a budget airline because its flight time suited my journey. This is exactly when a paid DragonPass membership should be useful. Instead, I’ve spent almost two hours in a queue and I’m still waiting.

I have used Aspire here before through Business Class access. The lounge is smaller than Escape, and the food selection is fine. The bigger issue is getting through the door in the first place.

If DragonPass members regularly face waits like this at Manchester T2, it is difficult to see what I am paying for. After years of membership, this is the airport where my DragonPass repeatedly fails to provide any practical benefit.

Nearly two hours waiting today, and the clock is still running.

user_reviews.Description:
I buy pizzas from here regularly and they're always really good. My only issue is with the chips.
For some reason, every order of chips comes covered in peri salt. I don't understand why peri salt is the default option. I personally don't like it, and neither does my family.
To avoid this, I now put "No peri salt" in the order notes and also tick the "No salt" option when ordering. Despite this, every order still arrives covered in peri salt and the chips end up going straight in the bin.
With the cost of living being what it is, I don't have money to waste on food that can't be eaten.
At weekends, when family visit and we order a takeaway, we've started ordering from elsewhere because of this issue.
No other takeaway I use automatically adds peri salt, which is why I find it so frustrating. Peri salt should be an optional extra for customers who want it, not the standard seasoning on every portion of chips.
The pizzas are great, but this ongoing issue is really putting us off ordering from Chesters.

Now, with these points in mind, you wouldn’t believe what happens next.

Ordered on uber eats, the order came and there was 3 chicken wings missing.

I called the restaurant, the man on the phone Bilal or whatever his name was, requested a name and address. I told him all of the above, including where i ordered - Uber eats. This experience with them is enough to make me never want to go back, not only was he rude and patronising, they will literally just laugh at you if it’s their mistake. not once did he apologise, offer a refund or to redeliver the next day.

i’m very disappointed, really unsure what happened to this place, but i most definitely will never return.

there is many many more takeaways that will actually value your hard earned money and service, please please please go there instead.

user_reviews.Name: jason hulme
user_reviews.Description:
First time ordering here and must say that we are very happy with our order.

We have seen the menu for here many times but never ordered before now.

We ordered using their app, you get a discount for using it.

The menu has a decent variety and the prices are very competitive. Make sure you check out the meal deals as most of them are cheaper than ordering the item on its own, i.e. the pizza meal deal is cheaper than ordering the same sized pizza on its own.

Delivery was good, within 40 mins. Food came hot and crucially everything was there and correct.

I liked that they kept the cans separate from the hot food so they were actually still cold when we got them. So many takeaways make the mistake of putting them in the same bag so you end up with luke warm pop, not good.

Food was tasty and the portion sizes are very good.

Overall impressed with this takeaway. We will be ordering again and if they can keep up the standard we got tonight, Chester's will probably become part of our goto takeaway list.

user_reviews.Name: Micky Watts
user_reviews.Description:
Wow. Honestly, Burger King, I would highly recommend that some regional management conduct an audit of the customer service staff working here. Absolutely disgusting behaviour. I think you would agree if you went there.

Firstly, my brother and I walked in and tried to use the electronic kiosk to order food. However, we noticed that only a takeaway option was available. Now my brother insisted that we sit in, so I said, "Well, we can ask the staff." He did this and was met with laughter from the staff. They said "yes" but rolled their eyes at the audacity of us wanting to sit in. God knows why my brother wanted to sit in, by the way, as the tables were messy and they couldn't even empty a bin between them. They were clearly rushed off their feet with the 4 customers in the place. In fact, including the 1 man on security, there were actually more staff members there than customers.

Now my brother is autistic, so he just thought they were friendly...THEY WEREN'T. Anyway, my brother took a while to decide what to get, and again I could see staff members laughing and again rolling their eyes at his choices. He wanted a milkshake, and it felt like he was asking them for a favour. Anyway, once they were done laughing at my brother, I decided I wanted to order a meal as well. Now it was my turn for some eye rolls.

Anyway, once I got my food, I joined my brother at the dirty table, as I said before, though they were clearly busy. It's at this point where I would like to apologise for interrupting STAFF MOVIE NIGHT, as there were 4 members of staff watching something on a phone. If I had known this, I would never have gone to Burger King and ruined their plans. Anyway, I felt bad about this, so I decided to clear the rubbish from our table and tried to put it in the overflowing bin.

In my time spent there (20 mins), I believe I did more work there than most of the staff on shift, just by clearing my table. Ultimately, I would highly recommend that management review these individuals, as I am confused about what they are being paid for. After seeing the recent reviews, I am also aware that I'm not the only person here with this opinion about customer service skills.

The only positive was that the food was fine, not bad, but not amazing, shame the same can't be said for the customer service and floor staff.

user_reviews.Name: Mahboubeh Bahmanpour
user_reviews.Description:
​To the Management,
​I am writing to express my strong disappointment regarding my recent order and the unacceptable experience at your restaurant.
​What I received was completely different from what I ordered, both in terms of visual presentation and pricing. First, I was overcharged at the till. Furthermore, the drink I ordered for my young daughter was displayed on the menu in a clear cup, showing a colorful, multi-layer beverage. However, it was served in a standard opaque paper cup usually used for carbonated soft drinks. This completely hid the colors of the drink, which was the whole reason my daughter chose it. As a result, she was upset and refused to drink it.
​Unfortunately, because my English is limited, my attempt to explain the pricing error and the mix-up to your staff was not understood. Instead of receiving assistance, we felt dismissed and left the restaurant feeling deeply dissatisfied and upset.
​I expect management to review this issue, address the overcharging, and ensure your staff provides better customer support when issues arise. I look forward to your response.

user_reviews.Name: Elle Taylor
user_reviews.Description:
We waited nearly an hour for our order, despite there only being two other people in the restaurant when we placed it (both delivery drivers).

After around 40 minutes, I asked about our order and was told it wasn’t ready. For approximately 20 minutes before this, I had noticed a bag sitting on the till, but nobody appeared to be calling for it. I then heard a member of staff say, “Oh, there it is,” while pointing at the bag. Around five minutes later, he asked me what drinks I had ordered before saying, “Oh, your order is here, we just needed to do the drinks.”

By this point, the food had been sitting on the till and had unfortunately gone cold, but we decided to take the order home anyway. When we arrived home, we realised that around half of the items were missing.

I returned to the restaurant with the order and explained what had happened to the manager. To be fair, the manager was very apologetic, extremely kind and dealt with the situation promptly. He offered to remake the missing items for us and resolved the issue without any further problems, which I really appreciated.

user_reviews.Name: Danny Waddicor
user_reviews.Description:
Extremely disappointing experience from start to finish.

We waited around 15–20 minutes after ordering before the food was finally brought out to the collection point. After that wait, you would at least expect the order to be fresh and correct — unfortunately, it was neither.

We ordered two children's cheeseburgers, yet somehow both arrived without any cheese. The entire order looked as though it had simply been thrown into the bag, with food loose and scattered everywhere. The kids' meals also weren't presented in the advertised meal boxes with the activity packs, which was another let-down.

Worst of all, the food was absolutely freezing and the overall quality was very poor. Spending approximately £25 on what is essentially cold, badly prepared fast food is simply unacceptable.

Burger King was way off the mark here. For the price, the McDonald's over the road offers far better value, better presentation and, based on this experience, a much more reliable standard.

Overall, a complete waste of money and an experience poor enough that we are very unlikely to return.

Popped in for a Chicken Royale and fries and honestly couldn't fault it. The burger was hot, fresh, and properly put together — not the flat, sad-looking thing you sometimes get at fast food places. Fries were crispy and came out at the right time too.

The place was also clean and well-kept — tables clear, floors tidy, which you don't always take for granted.
For the price, it's great value. Will definitely be back next time I'm in the area. Solid 5 stars from me! 🍔

user_reviews.Name: Bazour Esrifarni (Baz)
user_reviews.Description:
I am no stranger to writing reviews, and I usually try to be fair and balanced, but my recent experience at Costa Coffee deserves to be called out for what it was: overpriced, poor quality, and deeply disappointing.

I went in with two children, expecting a simple breakfast, nothing fancy, just enough to keep everyone fed and happy while out. Between us, we ordered two toasties, a croissant, two bottled drinks for the kids, and one hot chocolate. That was it. When the bill came, I was absolutely shocked to see the total: £22. For what was essentially a tray of snacks, this price is completely unjustifiable.

If the quality matched the cost, I might have let it go, but unfortunately, it was the opposite. The toasties were the biggest letdown. Both were undercooked, soggy, and barely warm in places. Instead of being crisp and golden with a gooey filling, they were limp and unpleasant to eat. For something so basic, it was inexcusable.

The croissant was no better, dry, stale, and heavy. Croissants should be light, flaky, and buttery. This one tasted like it had been sitting around all week, maybe longer. Honestly, I would have been disappointed with it even if I’d paid half the price.

The drinks weren’t much to write home about either. The kids had small bottled juices, which added disproportionately to the bill considering you can buy the same bottles in a supermarket for a fraction of the price. My hot chocolate was the only halfway decent item, but even then, it was more watery than rich, topped with a thin layer of cocoa powder. It was drinkable, yes, but certainly nothing special, especially when it makes up part of a £22 total.

What makes me most frustrated is that this is Costa, a brand that presents itself as a trusted high-street coffee shop where families can pop in for a reliable treat. But reliability means consistency, quality, and fair value. On this occasion, I got none of those. Instead, I left feeling ripped off, annoyed, and honestly a bit embarrassed that I’d just spent that amount of money for such a poor experience while trying to treat my children.

At £22, I could have taken the kids to a local independent café and had freshly prepared food, bigger portions, and change left over. In fact, for not much more I could have taken them to a sit-down family restaurant. Instead, I handed over a significant sum of money for food that felt rushed, carelessly made, and simply not worth it.

I don’t expect luxury from Costa, but I do expect value and decent preparation. Toasties should be hot, crisp, and cooked properly every time. Croissants should taste fresh. Drinks should feel like they’re worth what you’re paying. None of this happened, and the price tag only added insult to injury.

To be clear, I am not someone who complains for the sake of it, I write reviews regularly and I am fair when credit is due. But this was an experience where Costa badly failed, both in quality and in fairness. £22 for undercooked toasties, a stale croissant, two tiny juices, and a watery hot chocolate is nothing short of a rip-off.

I’ll be thinking twice before taking my children to Costa again. Families deserve better than this.

My review from few months ago :
"Can you please train your staff, new guy make me a latte not really hot, I asked him to do it a second time and it was almost the same, he wasn't able to use his machine correctly, also I had black dots in the latte. Frustrating. That happens to me again, I will avoid new staff now."

Nothing change, always the same guy, not trained. It becomes very frustrating. The milk must to be steamed not just making hot. And latte should have a bit foam on top

Information can help:
"Making hot milk just means heating it (like in a microwave or pan), while steaming milk uses pressurized steam to heat and aerate it, creating a silky, sweet, microfoam texture with tiny, integrated bubbles, perfect for lattes, whereas regular hot milk is simpler, and "frothed" milk (often confused with steamed) is fluffier with bigger, separate bubbles. Steaming transforms milk's proteins and fats, breaking them down for a smoother, sweeter, more stable liquid that blends beautifully with espresso, unlike just heating it which can scald the milk"

I spoke with the manager and another member of the staff remake my drink. Good customer service. All nice staff, just some need more training. Thanks again for the manager

user_reviews.Name: Ilyana Vilmozhna
user_reviews.Description:
Very disappointing experience at this Costa.

On 05 June 2026 at approximately 17:45 I visited this store to redeem a free drink reward from my Costa app. After scanning the reward, nothing happened and I simply asked for help.

Instead of assisting me, a staff member who identified herself as Julia became dismissive, refused to explain what was happening, refused to serve me, and refused to provide manager contact details when I requested them.

I am currently pregnant ( 20 week +) and left the store extremely upset and in tears. I have never experienced customer service like this in any Costa before.

A formal complaint has been submitted to Costa Head Office and I hope the matter is properly investigated.

user_reviews.Description:
We stopped at Costa for a little bite to eat before dinner, and (as usual) it was amazing. I got their December-exlusive Gingerbread Latte, along with a blueberry muffin; both these were fantastic! The Latte was really nice, I highly recommend getting it before it's gone until next year. It wasn't too loud for being open in a busy shopping centre, it was easy to hear everyone talk. Only issue is that there wasn't much table space, as we had to fit 6 of us around a small table, but that was only because it was quite full in there (just further shows that it's great food :D).
Anyways, great experience, great food, great service. Great!

user_reviews.Name: Jason Dugdale
user_reviews.Description:
Been meaning to try this place for a long time now and finally did.  I had the Delhi Spice special kebab and in terms of value, it’s outstanding. For under £8 you get doner, chicken tikka and a seek kebab all stir fried in their tomato tandoori sauce with onions placed on a fresh naan bread cooked in a tandoori clay oven.  Whilst the stir fry sauce is not overpowering, it disguises some of the individual flavours of the meat and I would best describe it as a sort of shashlik kebab. In terms of portion size, it’s very generous and comes with 2 tubs containing yoghurt mint sauce and a mild chilli sauce.  In terms of price, for the size of the kebab and the time taken to cook it in the sauce, the value is outstanding and it’s definitely a bargain.

The takeaway does a range of kebabs that are mostly stir fried but you can also have them not stir fried.  I don’t think this will be a regular takeaway for me but I shall certainly return in the future!

user_reviews.Name: Amy
user_reviews.Description:
Absolutely terrible customer service.

I went into this Costa with my work laptop, intending to sit for a while, grab a coffee and get some bits done. Shortly after I sat down, a staff member came over and asked me to leave because I hadn’t purchased anything yet. I explained that I was going to buy something, but was told that they “usually only give people around 15 minutes to purchase something.”

I have never heard of this 15-minute policy before. I go to Costa regularly, so I was quite taken aback by being spoken to in such a rude and dismissive tone.

I completely understand that a café may expect customers to purchase something if they want to use the seating, but I had every intention of buying something and could have simply been told this politely.

Instead, the interaction felt abrupt and unnecessarily unwelcoming. Although the seating is nice and the location is ideal and easy to get to after work, there are plenty of cafés where customers are treated with much more courtesy.

Very disappointing experience, and unfortunately not somewhere I would feel comfortable returning to.

user_reviews.Name: Nancy S
user_reviews.Description:
We spontaneously decided to eat out at this restaurant and we didn't regret it! First class service from all the staff and brilliant food.

The restaurant was quiet on a weekday but the traditional and nostalgic décor made it cosy to be in.

We ordered traditional Nepalese dishes such as Momocha and Nepalese Mixed Grill, and Karachi gosht as recommended, Paratha, and drinks.

The food was perfect; generous in portion, well spiced / seasoned, and delicious! They were all kept warm with their 'grill' on the table which made our dining experience even better! Reasonably priced too.

We enjoyed the meal and we'll definitely return when we decided to eat out again.

Highly recommended this restaurant!
